text:
leo: Heads-up — noticed a few GPU pods scheduled into the shared-gpu-pool this morning even though the deployment has the dedicated taint toleration. Latency spikes for other tenants. Anyone else seeing this?
anya: saw the alert on perf dashboard, +1. Which cluster/region?
leo: us-west-2 primary cluster. Affects model-serving-prod-* replicas. Spike started ~03:12 UTC.
sam: pasted pod YAML from one of the misrouted replicas: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: model-serving-prod-7f9d
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    accelerator: nvidia
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu/exclusive"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "true"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
          - key: "nodepool"
            operator: In
            values: ["dedicated-gpu"]
```
maria: hmm, that key looks suspicious — our taint on dedicated nodes is `gpu=exclusive:NoSchedule` (note `gpu` key, not `gpu/exclusive`). Looks like someone templated the toleration key incorrectly in the kustomize overlay.
leo: oh, that explains it. The toleration with `gpu/exclusive` wouldn't match `gpu` taint so scheduler put pods on any node with `accelerator: nvidia` nodeSelector.
infra-bot: [autoscaling-event] Node pool shared-gpu-pool scaled up +3 (reason: pending pods).
autoscaler-bot: suggestion: check pending pod tolerations and scale-down delay; current unneeded nodes countdown: 10m.
anya: quick mitigation ideas? We need to stop new replicas hitting shared pool and move existing ones if possible.
sam: we can patch deployments to add `nodeSelector: nodepool: dedicated-gpu` as a short-term force. Command: `kubectl patch deploy model-serving-prod -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"nodepool":"dedicated-gpu"}}}}}'`
maria: agree. Also we should rollout a kustomize fix to correct toleration key to `gpu` and push a canary. After that we can remove the temporary nodeSelector.
leo: is there a safer way to cordon the shared pool nodes while we fix templates? We don't want a mass eviction.
anya: can cordon + drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` but that evicts user pods — risky. Better to scale the deployment down/up in controlled batches on dedicated pool.
infra-bot: current count: 12 dedicated-gpu nodes healthy, 8 shared-gpu nodes. Dedicated has capacity for +20 pods at current load (estimated).
sam: I'll apply the nodeSelector patch as a canary to one deployment replica set, monitor, then roll the rest if green.
maria: follow-up task: add CI lint for toleration key pattern (must match `^gpu$`) and add an alert when pods with `accelerator: nvidia` land on non-dedicated nodepool.
leo: thanks team. I'm creating a short postmortem after we stabilize — capture root cause: template key typo + scheduler behavior + autoscaler reaction. :memo:
anya: ping @infra on the kustomize PR once it's ready, will review asap. :thumbsup:
